chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Saif al-Tammari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Some of our companions said to me: 'We used to shorten the daytime prayer when we stopped between the Maghrib and the later Isha.' He said: 'Allah knows best when He granted them concession. Allah has only prescribed for the traveler two rak'ahs, neither before them nor after them, except for the night prayer, on your camel wherever it takes you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing additional prayers before or after the traveler's two-rak'ah prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses a specific juristic debate regarding the traveler's prayer, clarifying that the divine concession of two rak'ahs is exclusive and precludes additional voluntary prayers (nafl) before or after, except for the night prayer (salat al-layl). The mention of praying on one's camel highlights the practical flexibility granted to travelers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease (yusr) in worship during journeys. This ruling underscores the distinction between obligatory shortened prayers and supererogatory acts, a key topic in Usul al-Fiqh discussions on the limits of travel concessions.
